subject: Post-call: pricing units & caching — follow-up and numbers
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: pricing units & caching — quick next steps

Hi Anna — thanks for the 30-min call just now. Quick write-up so we all have the same picture and a couple of concrete asks so we can size and propose.

Summary (what we heard)
- BrightWallet will use Redwood to power: transaction summary + customer support triage + 2 small analytic features (reranking).
- Estimated active users: 25k MAU; expected peak query load: ~150 qps for short chat-style requests.
- Typical prompt length (prompt + system): ~350 characters; average response target: ~900 characters.
- Important constraint: budget visibility up-front. Target economics: ~ $X / 1M tokens (we discussed needing to get to <$120 / 1M tokens blended).

Open questions / asks from us (please confirm):
1) Representative daily volume: you mentioned 6M–12M requests/month — can you confirm whether that is API calls (requests) or end-user sessions (which may contain multiple API calls)?
2) Cacheable traffic: how many of these requests are repetitive (identical prompt) vs dynamic per user? Even an approximate percentage (e.g., 30% repeated queries) helps a lot.
3) Procurement timeline & PO contact: please loop in procurement if you want us to produce a formal quote.

Why we asked about tokens vs characters vs requests
- Redwood pricing (hosted) bills per token. Third-party estimates you have may be per-character or per-request which leads to confusion when trying to map to your budget. Tokens are model-dependent and typically ~3–4 characters per token for English text, but that ratio changes with punctuation, code, etc.

Attachments: draft-pricing-units.xlsx (simple model) and a short explainer PDF on prompt caching behavior.

Next steps (recommended)
- Anna: confirm (1) whether your 6M–12M is calls or sessions and (2) estimated percent of repeat prompts.
- Redwood: after we get (1)+(2) we’ll send a 2-line unit economics table showing $/1M tokens for three fit scenarios (no cache / 30% cache / 60% cache) and a recommended model/quantization profile for cost vs latency.

Happy to jump on another 20-min call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — helpful recap. Two quick clarifications below.

1) Volume: when I said 6M–12M I was referring to API calls (individual model requests). We expect an average of ~8M calls/month for the first 6 months; could ramp to ~20M/mo in year 2.
2) Repeat prompts: for the support triage flow we expect a decent hit rate on repeat prompts (~35%) because many FAQ prompts are identical. For transaction summaries each request is unique (~5% repeat). Blended estimate ~22% repeat.

On the budget: our procurement lead asked whether "$ / 1M tokens" is the right way to reason — they have some vendors quoting per-1M characters or per-1k requests, and we want to compare apples-to-apples. Also, can you confirm whether repeated requests that are cached are billed the same?

I’ve CC’d procurement (procurement@brightwallet.com) to pull them in.

Hi Anna — great, thanks for the clarifications. Below is a short explainer + a worked example that maps characters/requests -> tokens and shows how caching affects billed tokens. I’ll attach the spreadsheet with the same calculations so procurement can tweak numbers.

Short explainer (tokens vs characters vs requests)
- Tokens: Redwood bills tokens. A token roughly ~3.2 characters on average for English prose (varies). Pricing *per token* is model-dependent; lighter quantized variants have different $/token.
- Characters: a vendor quoting per-character can be mapped to tokens by dividing characters by an estimated chars/token (we use 3.2 as a rule-of-thumb for prose).
- Requests: per-request pricing ignores payload size. If your requests are short (few tokens) per-request may look cheap; for long responses tokens dominate cost.

Prompt caching vs billed tokens (how caching actually helps)
- Cacheable dimension: Redwood can cache identical model inputs (the full prompt + system + function inputs) and replay the cached output without calling the model runtime. Cached hits are not billed for model tokens (you only pay minimal routing/storage cost).
- Important: caching depends on exact match. If you include volatile fields (timestamps, user IDs) in the prompt, cache hit rates fall. We recommend canonicalizing prompts or using template variables that are substituted server-side to increase cacheability.

Worked example (blended monthly, simple):
Inputs (blended):
- API calls/month: 8,000,000
- Average prompt chars: 350
- Average response chars: 900
- chars/token assumption: 3.2 -> prompt tokens ≈ 350 / 3.2 ≈ 110 tokens; response tokens ≈ 900 / 3.2 ≈ 281 tokens
- tokens per request (full): ~391 tokens/request
- blended cache hit rate: 22% (your number)

Scenario A — no cache: billed tokens/month = 8,000,000 * 391 ≈ 3,128,000,000 tokens
Scenario B — with 22% cache: billed tokens/month = 8,000,000 * 391 * (1 - 0.22) ≈ 2,439,840,000 tokens

Unit economics: convert to $/1M tokens (example pricing tiers for illustration only)
- If model A = $110 per 1M tokens -> Scenario A cost ≈ $344,080; Scenario B cost ≈ $268,382
- If model B (quantized) = $75 per 1M tokens -> Scenario A cost ≈ $234,600; Scenario B cost ≈ $183,489

Target metric: you asked about a target like <$120 / 1M tokens. For this workload we’d need either: (a) meaningful higher cache rates (~60%+) or (b) use a lower-cost model variant for high-volume paths + route quality-sensitive requests to higher-cost model. We can recommend an autoscaling routing policy to do exactly that.

Quick notes on per-request vendors: if a vendor quotes per-request, you must multiply by average tokens/request to compare. Example: $0.02 per request * 8M = $160k/mo regardless of payload size; if your requests are long this might be cheaper than a high per-token price but brittle as you scale payload size.

Attached: updated draft-pricing-units.xlsx with the three scenario rows (no-cache / 22% cache / 60% cache) and a tab with per-request equivalency math. Also attached the sample-prompt-cache-explainer.pdf which has recommended template approaches to raise cache hit rates.

Next steps from us
- We’ll produce two price views: 1) blended $/1M tokens for your current profile and 2) a routing/caching design that targets $<120/1M for the high-volume paths.
- Can procurement share target contract term (12/24 months) and any minimum commit? That impacts list discounts.

If useful we can also run a quick synthetic test against a sample of anonymized prompts to estimate the real token counts and cacheability — takes ~2 business days.

Cheers,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft-pricing-units.xlsx (updated), sample-prompt-cache-explainer.pdf
